lessons.title: Percentage from zero
lessons.explain: Percentage means 'per hundred'. 35% means 35 parts out of 100. It can also be written as a fraction or decimal.

examples.q: 40 out of 160 students passed. Find percentage.

lessons.mistakes: Do not confuse 'x% of y' with 'x/y'.

lessons.title: Percentage of a number
lessons.explain: Convert the percentage to a fraction whenever it gives easy cancellation.
lessons.shortcut: Cancel before multiplying.
lessons.mistakes: Do not multiply large numbers unnecessarily.

lessons.title: Increase and decrease
lessons.explain: An increase/decrease is always calculated from the current base value.
lessons.shortcut: For two changes a and b: net = a+b+ab/100; use negative sign for decrease.
lessons.mistakes: +20% and −20% do not cancel.

lessons.title: Reverse percentage
lessons.explain: If the final value and percentage change are known, work backward using the multiplier.
lessons.shortcut: Use 1.2, 0.8, 1.25, etc. for fast reverse calculation.
lessons.mistakes: Do not subtract 20% of the final value when reversing.

lessons.title: Meaning of ratio
lessons.explain: A ratio compares quantities in the same unit. 2:3 means 2 equal parts against 3 equal parts.
lessons.shortcut: Find one part before finding actual shares.
lessons.mistakes: Do not add actual quantities before checking the ratio.

lessons.title: Proportion
lessons.explain: Direct proportion: both quantities move together. Inverse proportion: one rises while the other falls.
lessons.visual:
More items → more cost
More workers → fewer days
lessons.rule: Direct x/y constant; inverse xy constant
lessons.shortcut: Ask first: same direction or opposite direction?
lessons.mistakes: Workers and days are normally inverse, not direct.

lessons.title: Average basics
lessons.explain: Average is the equal-share value. Add all values and divide by the number of values.
lessons.shortcut: For consecutive equally spaced values, the average is the middle value.
lessons.mistakes: Do not average averages unless group sizes are equal.

lessons.title: Combined and replacement average
lessons.explain: Convert averages back into totals before combining or replacing.
lessons.visual:
Average×count = total
change total → new average
lessons.shortcut: Track only the change when one member is replaced.
lessons.mistakes: Do not simply average 60 and 70.

lessons.title: CP, SP, profit and loss
lessons.explain: Cost Price is what you pay. Selling Price is what you receive.
lessons.visual:
CP → compare with SP
SP>CP profit
SP<CP loss
lessons.shortcut: Percent profit/loss is usually on CP.
lessons.mistakes: Do not calculate percentage on SP unless asked.

lessons.title: Discount
lessons.explain: Discount is calculated from Marked Price, then gives Selling Price.
lessons.shortcut: Successive discounts: a+b−ab/100.
lessons.mistakes: Do not add successive discounts directly.

lessons.title: Work as one unit
lessons.explain: Treat the complete job as 1. If A finishes in 10 days, A does 1/10 of the job each day.
lessons.visual:
One whole job = 1
A: 1/10 per day

examples.q: A finishes in 5 days. One day work?
A+B in 6 days, A in 10. B alone?

lessons.shortcut: Add work rates, not days.
lessons.mistakes: Do not add 10 and 15 days.

lessons.title: Efficiency
lessons.explain: More efficient means less time for the same work. Efficiency is inversely proportional to time.

examples.q: A takes 12 days, B is twice as efficient

lessons.shortcut: Double efficiency means half the time.
lessons.mistakes: Do not keep the same ratio for time.

lessons.title: The core triangle
lessons.explain: Distance, speed and time are connected. Keep units consistent.
lessons.visual:
D = S × T
S = D/T
T = D/S
lessons.shortcut: km/h → m/s multiply by 5/18.
lessons.mistakes: Never mix minutes with hours.

lessons.title: Relative speed
lessons.explain: When objects move toward each other, speeds add. Same direction, subtract.
lessons.shortcut: Draw arrows before choosing add/subtract.
lessons.mistakes: Same direction usually means difference.

lessons.title: Simple Interest
lessons.explain: Interest is calculated on the original principal every period.
lessons.visual:
P stays unchanged
same interest each year
lessons.shortcut: At 10%, yearly interest=P/10.
lessons.mistakes: Do not add interest to principal for SI.

lessons.title: Compound growth
lessons.explain: Each period earns interest on the previous amount.
lessons.shortcut: Use multiplier 1.1,1.2,0.9 for speed.
lessons.mistakes: Do not use SI formula for multiple compounded periods.

lessons.title: Difference patterns
lessons.explain: First check differences between terms. If differences change regularly, check second differences.
lessons.rule: Test the rule on at least two gaps.
lessons.shortcut: Check differences before complex patterns.
lessons.mistakes: Do not accept a rule based on one jump.

lessons.title: BODMAS clearly
lessons.explain: Solve brackets, powers/orders, then multiplication/division left-to-right, then addition/subtraction.
lessons.rule: Same priority operations go left to right.
lessons.shortcut: Division and multiplication have equal priority.
lessons.mistakes: Do not do addition before multiplication.

lessons.title: Compass and turns
lessons.explain: Draw a compass every time. Right/left changes after every turn.
lessons.shortcut: Use arrows, not imagination alone.
lessons.mistakes: Do not use page-right after the person turns.

lessons.title: Final direction
lessons.explain: Cancel opposite movements and then inspect the remaining horizontal and vertical movement.
lessons.shortcut: Cancel first, decide direction second.
lessons.mistakes: Total distance is not needed when direction is asked.

lessons.title: Family tree method
lessons.explain: Convert every statement into a tree. First identify generation, then gender.
lessons.rule: Translate one relation at a time.

examples.q: P father of Q; Q sister of R
A sister of B; B father of C

lessons.shortcut: Draw instead of remembering long chains.
lessons.mistakes: Sibling does not tell gender unless stated.

lessons.title: Circle logic
lessons.explain: All means one set inside another; No means separate; Some means at least one overlap.
lessons.visual:
All A are B: A inside B
No A is B: separate
lessons.rule: Accept only conclusions forced by statements.

examples.q: All cats animals; all animals living
Some pens books; all books useful
No A is B; Some B are C

lessons.shortcut: Draw circles quickly.
lessons.mistakes: Some does not mean all.

lessons.title: Build a comparison chain
lessons.explain: Write all relations as one chain where possible.
lessons.shortcut: Use one written chain.
lessons.mistakes: Do not reverse signs accidentally.

lessons.title: Test transformations
lessons.explain: Compare every character. Check +/− shifts, reversal and alphabet positions.
lessons.rule: Verify the rule on all examples.
lessons.shortcut: Confirm with more than one letter.
lessons.mistakes: Do not invent a pattern that works once.

lessons.title: Rank formula
lessons.explain: If the same person is counted from both sides, subtract one duplicate.
lessons.shortcut: The person is counted twice before subtracting one.
lessons.mistakes: Do not simply add ranks.

lessons.title: Linear arrangement
lessons.explain: Create slots first. Put fixed positions before relative clues.

examples.q: A not at ends; B immediately left of A

lessons.shortcut: Make blocks for 'immediately'.
lessons.mistakes: Do not place 'next to' as one fixed order.

lessons.title: Circular arrangement
lessons.explain: Choose one person as reference when relative positions matter, then place clockwise/counterclockwise.
lessons.visual:
Fix A at top
→ clockwise positions
lessons.rule: Relative placement is enough unless facing rules change.

examples.q: B is immediate right of A, all face centre
steps: Right means counterclockwise when facing centre

lessons.shortcut: Write F-center/F-outside before solving.
lessons.mistakes: Left/right reverses for people facing the centre.

lessons.title: Floor and box puzzles
lessons.explain: Make a table of floors/boxes and fill direct clues first. Use blanks for variables.
lessons.rule: Fixed clue → negative clue → conditional clue

examples.q: B above C; A not on top/bottom

lessons.shortcut: Write every restriction beside the table.
lessons.mistakes: Do not solve mentally when clues exceed two.

lessons.title: Know the job of the word
lessons.explain: A word's part of speech depends on its job in the sentence.
lessons.visual:
Noun=name
Pronoun=replaces
Verb=action/state
Adjective=describes noun
Adverb=modifies
lessons.rule: Ask: what is this word doing?

examples.q: She quickly completed the difficult task.

lessons.shortcut: Ask what the word modifies.
lessons.mistakes: The same word can have different roles in different sentences.

lessons.title: Simple present
lessons.explain: Use for habits, routines, facts and schedules.
lessons.visual: every day / usually / always → simple present
lessons.shortcut: Look for routine words.
lessons.mistakes: Do not add -s after I/you/we/they.

lessons.title: Continuous tenses
lessons.explain: Use be + verb-ing for an action in progress.
lessons.visual:
am/is/are + ing = present
was/were + ing = past
lessons.rule: Choose be verb by subject and time.
lessons.shortcut: Look for now, while, at that moment.
lessons.mistakes: Do not use base verb after is/are in continuous form.

lessons.title: Find the true subject
lessons.explain: The verb agrees with the main subject, not a nearby noun in an 'of' phrase.

examples.q: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.

lessons.shortcut: Temporarily remove extra phrases to expose the subject.
lessons.mistakes: Do not match the verb with the nearest noun automatically.

lessons.title: A, An and The
lessons.explain: Choose a/an by sound. Use 'the' for a specific or already mentioned noun.
lessons.visual:
an apple (vowel sound)
a university ('you' sound)
an honest man (silent h)

examples.q: I saw a dog. ___ dog was friendly.

lessons.shortcut: Say the word aloud when unsure.
lessons.mistakes: Do not choose an just because the first letter is a vowel.

lessons.title: Pronoun reference
lessons.explain: A pronoun replaces a noun and must clearly point to the correct antecedent.
lessons.shortcut: Find the noun being replaced first.
lessons.mistakes: Do not let a nearby noun confuse the reference.

lessons.title: Place and time relationships
lessons.explain: Prepositions connect things by place, time or direction.
lessons.visual:
at 5 PM
on Monday
in June
lessons.shortcut: Group phrases together: at night, on Monday, in 2026.
lessons.mistakes: Do not translate word-for-word from another language.

lessons.title: Joining ideas
lessons.explain: Conjunctions join words or clauses and show relationships.

examples.q: I stayed because it was raining.

lessons.shortcut: Read both halves of the sentence.
lessons.mistakes: Do not choose only by memorised translation.

lessons.title: Systematic checking
lessons.explain: Check one grammar area at a time instead of reading randomly.
lessons.rule: Read → split → test grammar → reread meaning

examples.q: The list of items are ready.
Each of the players have a jersey.

lessons.shortcut: Check the main subject first.
lessons.mistakes: Do not assume the plural noun after 'of' controls the verb.

lessons.title: Meaning first, grammar second
lessons.explain: Read the whole passage before filling blanks. Then use context, grammar and collocation.
lessons.rule: The sentence around the blank is evidence.
lessons.shortcut: Read the completed sentence again.
lessons.mistakes: Do not answer each blank without reading context.

lessons.title: Find the opening and links
lessons.explain: Look for a general opening, pronoun references, connectors and logical sequence.
lessons.rule: Pronouns usually need an earlier noun.

examples.q: Sentence B starts 'This method...' while A introduces the method.
However shows contrast with previous statement.

lessons.shortcut: Build mandatory pairs first.
lessons.mistakes: A sentence starting with 'this/these/they' rarely opens.

lessons.title: Read for structure
lessons.explain: First identify the passage topic, author's purpose and paragraph roles. Then answer from evidence.
lessons.rule: Answer what is supported, not what you personally know.
lessons.shortcut: Return to the relevant lines for evidence.
lessons.mistakes: Do not use outside knowledge.
